memoryText: He who testifies to these things says, Surely I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus! The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all. Amen.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Revelation 22:20-21 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These are the last words of the Bible, and they are a prayer. After sixty-six books, after every promise, warning, and story, the book ends with a longing: “Come, Lord Jesus!”

The words belong to Jesus first: “Surely I am coming soon.” He promises. And then the church answers: “Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!” We do not just wait; we long. This is not a nervous prayer but the prayer of a bride for her husband.

And then, a benediction: “The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.” The Bible, which opens with creation, ends with grace. We have no claim on God but this: the unearned favor of the Lord Jesus. Everything depends on it.

Pray these words today, and let your longing for his return increase. Come, Lord Jesus.
weekInReview: This week you reached the climax of Revelation. Chapters 17 and 18 showed the fall of Babylon, the world system drunk with the blood of the saints, and the call to come out of her. Chapter 19 gave the marriage supper of the Lamb and the rider on the white horse, Faithful and True, with the word of God as his sword. Chapter 20 showed Satan bound, the thousand years (understood in three main ways), and the great white throne. On Day 892, we paused on the final judgment, in which Christ judges with justice, and those in him are not condemned. Chapters 21 and 22 showed the new heavens and new earth, with God dwelling with his people, no more tears, the tree of life, the river, and the sight of his face. On Day 894, we paused on the hope of a renewed creation. And Revelation 22:6-21 gave the final words of the Bible: Jesus is coming soon, the thirsty may take the water of life, and the church prays, “Come, Lord Jesus.”
reflectionQuestions: Revelation 18 shows Babylon’s wealth built partly on trafficking in human lives. What do you see in your own culture or economy that resembles this, and what is one concrete thing you can do about it?
Revelation 21:3-4 promises God’s dwelling with us, no more tears, and no more death. Which of these promises means the most to you today, and who in your life needs to hear it?
The Bible ends with the prayer, “Come, Lord Jesus!” Do you pray this, and mean it? What are the things that make you hold on to this world, and what would it look like to long for his coming more?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for rest and for the hope of his return.
